messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: [Recap] Batching & token-econ — decision sync and pilot next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard, the levers we think move the needle, and proposed next steps so your procurement and ML Ops leads have something tangible to react to.

Summary of pain / goals (from our call)
- Per-token spend is the biggest blocker; finance flagged a hard cap for Q3 inference spend (~€40k/mo).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for interactive scoring flows.
- Mixed traffic: 60% short conversational prompts, 40% long-form synthesis (avg 300 tokens).
- Audit/compliance: SOC2 and request-level audit logs are required for pilot.

Levers & preliminary economics (back-of-envelope)
- Batching + dynamic aggregation: expected token-cost reduction 20–30% for your request mix (see attached batching-sim.csv).
- Prefix/KV caching for repeat prompts: ~10–15% additional savings on heavy repeats (user templates).
- Model routing: small/medium model variants for low-complexity paths -> incremental 10–20% CPU/GPU time savings; tradeoff testing in pilot.
- Quantization + int8 runtime on dedicated hosts: one-time performance uplift, reduces token cost further for sustained traffic.

Estimated blended saving range: 35–50% vs current baseline depending on how many requests qualify for caching/routing. We’ll validate with a 2-week bench + 2-week live pilot.

Proposed next steps (decision calendar)
1) We run a 2-week benchmarking pass on a 100k-sample of production requests you provide (sample due: Jul 14). Outputs: per-route latency, per-token cost, and recommended batching window.
2) Pilot (4 weeks): scoped to 1–2 routes, real traffic shadow + gradual cutover. Success criteria: maintain p95 <200ms, achieve >=30% token cost reduction vs baseline, and produce audit logs.
3) Commercial options: month-to-month usage or a 6-mo reserved commit with deeper discounts if you can commit to a throughput floor.

Attachments: batching-sim.csv (simulated cost model), token_runbook.xlsx (sample mapping + metric defs). I’ll also drop a short proposal PDF after we sync with procurement.

Can you confirm:
- Sample requests availability by Jul 14?
- Procurement timeline (legal + security) target — do you have a procurement owner we should loop in?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the bench run with Dev once you confirm dates.

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

- Procurement: legal/security owner is Priya (cc’d). Typical procurement window is 3–4 weeks for a pilot (security questionnaire + SOC2 review). If the pilot terms are straightforward, we can expedite.

- Budget: Finance is flexible if the ROI forecast is concrete. They asked for a sample breakdown showing per-route monthly run-rate at projected savings (we’ll need this to justify a commit).

One more ask: can Dev come to a 30-minute technical sync with our ML infra team next Tue (Jul 14) at 10:00 CET? That’s when we’ll hand off the sample.
